title: Sputum as a named specimen, not a diagnosis
dek: Wikipedia's sputum page is mucus from the lower airway. Quality, induction, and smear/NAAT logic stay on clinic plates.
story: Sputum on Wikipedia is a specimen type: lower-airway secretions, not saliva. TB laboratories live and die on that distinction.
Induced sputum, gastric aspirate, stool as a pediatric WRD specimen — those are clinic-module objects. This card is the named thing people cough.
A beautiful Wikipedia diagram of a mucopurulent sample does not grade smear or call RIF.
deep: Blood-streaked sputum is still sputum (hemoptysis card).
Volume folklore is less important than getting a real lower-airway sample and a WRD.
Infection-control plates own how you collect it.

visual.caption: Specimen first, then test class. Saliva is a failed start, not a negative TB test.
